TASK: Rework `/dashboard/new` so its prompt box IS the homepage prompt box, and so the two helper flows open in place instead of navigating away.

READ FIRST:
1. `docs/design-system.md` — binding contract.
2. `components/marketing/PromptHero.tsx` IN FULL — the homepage prompt box. This is the thing to port: its styling, its glow-ring treatment, and its **voice-to-text** (Web Speech API, mic button, with a `useSyncExternalStore` support probe so the button never renders on the server). The glow uses `.glow-clip-a/-b` + `.glow-spin-a/-b` in `app/globals.css` — read the long comment there, it explains why the technique is what it is and what was already tried and rejected.
3. `app/(portal)/dashboard/new/**` — the current Create page: `page.tsx`, `CreateFlow.tsx`, `Composer.tsx`, `BuildLaunch.tsx`, `build-steps.ts`, `image.ts`. This is careful work; you are changing the composer, not the build-launch machinery.
4. `components/templates/TemplatePickerModal.tsx` and `components/wizard/InlineWizard.tsx` — two components being built RIGHT NOW by other agents. **Their interfaces are pinned and will not change.** Read the exported types.

YOU OWN: `app/(portal)/dashboard/new/**` only. **Do NOT edit** `components/marketing/PromptHero.tsx` (the homepage uses it), `components/templates/**`, `components/wizard/**`, or anything else. If you need code out of PromptHero, COPY it into your own file — do not refactor theirs.

## THE FOUR CHANGES

**1. Port the homepage prompt box exactly.** Same styling, same glow ring, same voice-to-text. The owner was explicit: "keep the exact same prompt box that we have from the homepage, styling, glow effects, the voice to text."

Copy rather than import, and say in a comment why (PromptHero is a marketing component with its own concerns — sessionStorage stashing, the auth wall, a rewards pill — that do not belong on a page where the customer is already signed in). Keep the two files' shared behaviour recognisably identical so a future change to one prompts a look at the other.

**2. Remove the reference-image attachment.** The owner wants the "add a reference image" button and its explanatory text gone from this page. Note the image path is genuinely real end-to-end, so this is a product decision, not a correctness one — remove the UI cleanly and **do not leave dead code behind**. If `image.ts` becomes unused, say so in your report; do not delete it without checking for other callers.

**3. "Use a template" opens `TemplatePickerModal` in place** — a modal over this page, not a navigation to `/dashboard/templates`. On `onComplete`, put the returned `prompt` in the composer, editable, and carry `logoDataUrl` and `palette` through to the build.

**4. "Help me write it" opens `InlineWizard` in place** — not a navigation to `/wizard`. Same hand-off: prompt into the composer, editable.

For both: the returned prompt must be **visible and editable before anything is built**. Neither may auto-submit.

## CARRYING logo AND palette THROUGH

Both components can return `logoDataUrl` (a data URL) and `palette` (hex strings). Work out honestly what the build can actually do with them:
- Read `app/api/generate/route.ts` for what it accepts. The image field is validated against `/^data:(image\/(?:png|jpeg|webp));base64,/` and reaches the model on **attempt 1 only**.
- Read `lib/brand-kit.ts` for how palette/brand is represented and whether a build already consumes it.

**If a returned value cannot actually reach the build, do not silently drop it** — either wire it properly, or fold it into the prompt text so it still influences the result, and say which you did. Do not accept a logo from the customer and then discard it.

## HARD RULES
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.**
- The mic button must not render during SSR (`getSpeechRecognition()` is `window`-only) and must degrade silently where the Web Speech API is absent — PromptHero already solves this; copy the solution, do not reinvent it.
- `k-focus` on every interactive element (note: `k-focus-within` exists for controls whose real input is visually hidden). `k-num` on figures.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` — the glow animations are already covered by the global rule; do not add motion that escapes it.
- Keep the existing honest credit copy: the range not a quote, the balance-checked-only-at-start warning, the spend-cap callouts.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0`, and `node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` (315 currently pass). Run all three.
- A dev server is running on port 3003. Use it; do not start another. **Actually render the page** — this is one of the few pages that can be checked without a login wall issue, and the glow ring in particular has a history of not appearing in practice despite looking correct in source. Verify it renders.

REPORT BACK: what you ported and what you deliberately left behind, whether the glow actually rendered, what you did with logo and palette, whether `image.ts` is now orphaned, and anything untested.

1	# Kodely product design system
2	
3	The contract for the customer-facing portal (`app/(portal)/**`) and the builder
4	(`app/projects/[id]/**`). Marketing pages (`app/page.tsx`, `/pricing`, `/blog`,
5	`/templates`, `/wizard`) are a **separate** system — do not repoint their tokens.
6	
7	## The one-sentence brief
8	
9	An AI website builder that happens to have a customer portal around it — not a
10	dashboard that happens to contain a builder. The primary action is always
11	"build something".
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Tokens
16	
17	Defined in `app/globals.css`, exposed to Tailwind via `@theme inline`. **Use the
18	Tailwind class, never a raw hex and never an arbitrary-value bracket.**
19	
20	### Surface
21	
22	| Class | Use |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `bg-canvas` | The page behind panels. Set by `AppShell`; pages never set it. |
25	| `bg-surface` | Cards, panels, the sidebar. |
26	| `bg-surface-2` | Hover, inset rows, quiet fills. |
27	| `bg-surface-3` | Track of a progress bar, the deepest step. |
28	| `bg-inset` | Code/preview wells. |
29	
30	### Line
31	
32	`border-hair` (default for cards) · `border-line-mid` (inputs, menus) ·
33	`border-line-strong` (emphasis, pending step outline)
34	
35	### Text
36	
37	`text-ink` (primary) · `text-ink-2` (secondary/body) · `text-ink-3` (tertiary,
38	placeholder, disabled) · `text-ink-inv` (on a brand fill)
39	
40	### Brand
41	
42	`text-brand` `bg-brand` `bg-brand-tint` `bg-brand-tint-2` `text-brand-ink`
43	
44	`--brand-gradient` is a **fill of last resort**. Exactly one element per view may
45	carry it: the primary button. Do not gradient headings, cards, borders or icons.
46	
47	### Status
48	
49	`ok` `warn` `danger` `info`, each with a `-tint` companion
50	(`text-ok` / `bg-ok-tint`). Status colour is never the brand colour.
51	
52	### Radius / elevation / motion
53	
54	`rounded-sm|md|lg|xl|2xl` (8/10/14/20/28px) · `shadow-e1|e2|e3` ·
55	`duration-[var(--t-1)]` 120ms, `--t-2` 200ms, `--t-3` 380ms ·
56	`ease-[var(--ease)]`
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Utility classes
61	
62	`k-focus` — **put this on every interactive element.** One focus ring, product-wide.
63	`k-display` `k-h1` `k-h2` `k-label` — the type scale. `k-label` is the only uppercase.
64	`k-num` — **required** on any figure: credits, prices, counts, dates in a column.
65	`k-scroll-x` — wrap any wide table/code block. The page body must never scroll sideways.
66	`k-msg-in` `k-step-in` `k-step-active` — entrance and progress animations.
67	`k-preview-busy` / `k-preview-idle` — the preview treatment while the AI works.
68	`k-wash` — ambient brand glow inside a hero panel. Sparingly: one per page, at most.
69	`k-gradient-border` — gradient hairline. Reserve for the single most important panel.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Components (`components/ui/`)
74	
75	Import these. **Do not hand-roll a second version of any of them.**
76	
77	| Component | Notes |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| `Button` `ButtonLink` `IconButton` `buttonClass` | Variants `primary\|secondary\|ghost\|soft\|danger`, sizes `xs\|sm\|md\|lg`. **One `primary` per view.** `IconButton` requires `label`. |
80	| `Card` `CardHeader` `SectionHeader` | `interactive` only if it truly responds. |
81	| `Badge` | `tone` + `dot` + `pulse`. Set `dot` on anything conveying live state — colour alone is not a status channel. |
82	| `Input` `Textarea` `Select` `SearchInput` | Label/hint/error/aria wiring is built in. Never hand-write a bare `<input>`. |
83	| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
84	| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
85	| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
86	| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
87	| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
88	| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
89	| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
90	| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
91	| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
92	| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
93	| `Spinner` | |
94	
95	## Shell (`components/app/`)
96	
97	`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
98	drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
99	supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
100	`ToastProvider`, and no page sets a title suffix (the group layout owns the
101	`"%s — Kodely"` template; a page declares only its own noun).
102	
103	Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
104	once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.
105	
106	`SidebarFooter` carries the brand-gradient credits card, the theme toggle and
107	the bug/feature link (`/support?topic=bug`, `?topic=feature`). It appears in
108	both the desktop rail and the mobile drawer.
109	
110	**The credits card has no progress bar and no "X of Y" figure, deliberately.**
111	There is no allowance for the balance to be a fraction of — credits are bought
112	in packs and never expire — so a bar would have to invent a denominator. It
113	shows the balance and "about N more builds" from `averageBuildCredits()`.
114	**Anything else in the product showing credits must agree with it.** A card
115	elsewhere claiming a monthly total would contradict the rail sitting beside it.
116	
117	### Where the brand gradient may be used as a fill
118	
119	Three places, and nowhere else: the single `primary` button on a view, the
120	sidebar credits card, and the `/support` credits card. Not on headings, cards,
121	borders, icons or section dividers.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## AI progress is one object, not three spinners
126	
127	`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
128	an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
129	same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.
130	
131	**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
132	its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
133	build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
134	agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
135	and not a progress bar.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)
140	
141	| Thing | Reality |
142	| --- | --- |
143	| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
144	| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |
145	| **Invoices / payment method** | Not fetched from Stripe. The credit ledger is the only history. |
146	| **Thumbnails** | Nothing captures a screenshot. No headless browser. |
147	| **Project status** | Only `publishedAt` → Published / Draft. No `archived`. "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = RUNNING` but has no staleness rule, so it is not yet trustworthy. |
148	| **Domains** | No model, no field, no route. Sites live at `<slug>.kodely.site` only. |
149	| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |
150	| ~~**Support tickets**~~ | **NOW BUILT.** `SupportTicket` + `SupportMessage` exist, with customer-visible staff replies. `SupportNote` remains a separate, admin-only internal note that is still never shown to the customer — do not conflate them. Tickets are included in the data export and the deletion preview; if you add a field holding a customer's words, both must be updated too. |
151	| **Storage / bandwidth** | Not measured anywhere. |
152	| **Workspaces / members / roles** | No concept of it. Ownership is one FK: `Project.userId`. |
153	| **Avatar upload, password change, 2FA, notification prefs** | None. |
154	
155	**Sessions list and revoke, and editing `User.name`, are now BUILT** — see
156	`/settings/security` and `/settings`. Note what `Session` actually records:
157	`id · userId · tokenHash · expiresAt · createdAt`, and nothing else. There is no
158	user agent, no IP, no last-seen and no device. Do not add a column for them
159	casually: `/legal/rights` and the data export both enumerate in writing
160	everything the database holds, so a new personal-data field silently makes two
161	published documents wrong.
162	
163	### The rule
164	
165	A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
166	that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
167	Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.
